name: Raw meat / raw liver diet

image.caption: Raw Pork Meat in Bloody Butchery of Corpses

lead: The raw meat or raw liver diet means eating animal foods, including organs such as liver and heart, uncooked. Followers on looksmax.org are after fuller physical development, better skin and sturdier bones, which they link to higher natural IGF-1 and growth hormone.

The idea is that raw animal foods keep nutrients that cooking degrades, and that those nutrients support the body's own growth signalling. No human trials have tested the diet for appearance outcomes. Raw liver is a rich source of vitamins and minerals, including preformed vitamin A.

paras: Members describe plans built around raw milk products, raw organs such as liver and heart, raw meat and fish, and occasional fruit with few or no vegetables. It is usually followed as an all-in eating pattern over months rather than a single add-on, and some members say they follow it to support development during puberty. Other members call it TikTok hype.

Reviews and case reports link raw liver to tapeworm infection, fascioliasis, toxoplasmosis, toxocariasis and halzoun syndrome, and undercooked pork products to hepatitis E. Thorough cooking kills parasites, viruses and most bacteria. A single slice of beef liver can exceed the tolerable upper intake for preformed vitamin A. Pregnant people, children and anyone with a weakened immune system face the highest risk from foodborne infection.

chain: More growth, better skin and bones
angle.text: Followers eat raw meat, organs and dairy expecting more natural IGF-1 and growth hormone, which they link to better skin, stronger bones and fuller physical development. The expected gains come from proponents' theory and personal reports; the medical literature in this area mainly describes infections tied to raw liver and undercooked meat.

lead: The raw meat or raw liver diet involves eating meat, organs and often dairy uncooked. One looksmax.org member describing his plan listed raw milk products, raw organs such as liver, hearts and bones, raw meat and fish, and occasional fruit with no vegetables, citing natural IGF-1 production, increased growth hormone and skin endurance as expected benefits. [1]

Other members argue the approach is hype from TikTok and could affect health during puberty. [2] No published trials have examined raw meat or raw liver diets in people for appearance or health outcomes.

The medical literature documents infections tied to raw liver and undercooked meat, including tapeworm in Taiwanese communities that ate raw wild boar liver, toxoplasmosis outbreaks in Korea after raw pig liver or spleen, and halzoun syndrome from raw sheep liver in the Eastern Mediterranean. [3] Wikipedia reports that thorough cooking kills parasites, viruses and most bacteria. [4]
infobox: Raw meat, organs (liver, heart), sometimes raw dairy [1]

paras: The diet overlaps with carnivore and primal eating but specifies that animal foods be uneaten cooked, often with an emphasis on organ meats. [1] Raw liver appears in several traditional cuisines, for example Lebanese asbeh nayeh and Japanese liver sashimi, according to Wikipedia. [5]

Wikipedia reports that animal liver is rich in iron, copper, B vitamins and preformed vitamin A, and that a single 68 g slice of beef liver exceeds the tolerable upper intake for preformed vitamin A. [5]

No studies found of raw meat or raw liver diets in people. Related research is limited to infection reports and veterinary studies on raw feeding of cats, which are not evidence about human appearance or health.

A historical review of Taenia asiatica in Taiwan attributes high tapeworm prevalence among aboriginal communities to a culture of eating raw liver from hunted wild boar.  Two Korean toxoplasmosis outbreaks followed meals of raw wild pig spleen and liver and raw domestic pig liver. [6] A case report and review of halzoun syndrome describes nasopharyngeal symptoms after raw sheep liver in the Eastern Mediterranean and advises counseling on the hazards of raw liver in endemic areas.

A review of human fascioliasis lists raw liver ingestion among risk factors. [7] A familial case of visceral toxocariasis was linked to raw bovine liver. [8] Hepatitis E reviews state that infections occur through eating undercooked meat from pigs, boar and deer. [9] A French study found matching hepatitis E virus sequences in humans with locally acquired infection and in swine livers. [10]
Wikipedia notes that Salmonella, E. coli O157:H7 and Campylobacter are common bacterial causes of foodborne illness and that infants, young children and travelers are particularly vulnerable. [4]
Posts on looksmax.org range from members planning raw diets and documenting them, to a thread arguing raw meat is hype and may affect development during puberty. [1][2]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, raw meat diets are posted about as a primal approach to growth and skin, and are disputed by other members. [1][2]
